summary: Philip A. Kuhn worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown, and served in the U.S. Armed Forces before holding posts at the University of Chicago and Harvard University.

Philip A. Mellor is a religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. In 2010, he was Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip Boas Yampolsky specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor and librarian at Columbia and chair of the Numata Center.

Philip Clart is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from around 1991 to 1996. Around 2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.
Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was also attested as a teaching associate in 2020.

Philip Kapleau worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Daiun Harada, and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, and founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh, later holding posts at Brown University and the University of Notre Dame as John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy.

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. from the University of Chicago. He joined the University of Iowa in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who earned a BA from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center.

Philipp A. Maas specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn, supervised by Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler, and held research and teaching posts at Bonn, Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig.

Philippe Stern was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments at the Musée Guimet (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste around 1928, and the École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from McGill University, where his doctoral supervisor was G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and studied under Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, Richard P. Hayes, and several other teachers.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1838. He was a professor of Tibetan at INALCO and later served as Professeur de Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1857–1894).

Phillip E. Bloom works in sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University around 2013 under the doctoral supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, and by 2012 served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Brahmapundit works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat, President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities, and Chairperson of the International Council for the Day of Vesak.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. In 2013, he was an associate professor at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney around 2009 under Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle. He also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts in 2015 as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.
